pattern.name: batch_rename
pattern.description: Template for batch file renaming operations
pattern.bash_example: #!/bin/bash # Batch rename with pattern replacement find "$SOURCE_DIR" -name "$PATTERN" -type f | while read -r file; do new_name=$(echo "$file" | sed "s/$OLD_PATTERN/$NEW_PATTERN/g") echo "Renaming: $file -> $new_name" mv "$file" "$new_name" done
pattern.python_example:
import os import re from pathlib import Path
def batch_rename(directory, pattern, replacement, recursive=True): """Batch rename files using regex patterns""" path = Path(directory) for file_path in path.rglob('*') if recursive else path.iterdir(): if file_path.is_file() and re.search(pattern, file_path.name): new_name = re.sub(pattern, replacement, file_path.name) new_path = file_path.parent / new_name print(f"Renaming: {file_path} -> {new_path}") file_path.rename(new_path)

pattern.name: organize_by_date
pattern.description: Organize files into date-based folder structure
pattern.bash_example: #!/bin/bash # Organize files by modification date find "$SOURCE_DIR" -type f | while read -r file; do date_dir=$(date -r "$file" +%Y-%m) mkdir -p "$TARGET_DIR/$date_dir" mv "$file" "$TARGET_DIR/$date_dir/" done

pattern.name: extract_metadata
pattern.description: Extract and use file metadata for organization
pattern.bash_example: #!/bin/bash # Extract PDF metadata and rename for file in *.pdf; do title=$(pdfinfo "$file" | grep "Title:" | cut -d: -f2- | sed 's/^ *//') author=$(pdfinfo "$file" | grep "Author:" | cut -d: -f2- | sed 's/^ *//') if [ -n "$title" ] && [ -n "$author" ]; then new_name="${author}_${title}.pdf" new_name=$(echo "$new_name" | tr ' ' '_' | tr -d '[:punct:]') mv "$file" "$new_name" fi done
